about: P6 Concourse building designs, one per building, written 27 Nov 2026 (proposed). Front row (P6-01 to P6-07) runs from the Concourse Road (low y) to Hotel Row (high y); the hotel row (P6-10 to P6-15) runs from Hotel Row (low y) to the Station Road (high y). The Concourse Promenade crosses between Transit Lounges and Market Hall. Coordinates in metres from each lot's bow-port corner.

buildings.name: Greeters' Hall

parts.name: Greeting hall
parts.room: Greeting hall (meeting point under the light roof)

buildings.structure: Steel space-frame roof, 21 m (69 ft) high, on eight tree columns; concrete service wing.
buildings.look: A tall, airy hall under a glowing white space-frame roof with big arrival boards, glass on all sides; meeting crowds are visible from the street.
buildings.entrances: Arrivals come in under the canopy from the terminals; doors to the waiting garden on Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 5,000 people waiting at a time.
buildings.services: Arrival boards linked to every gate, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: One great greeting hall where people meet arriving travellers, with welcome desks, gift shops, cafés, lost and found and a family room in the service wing and a gallery lounge above, and a waiting garden behind.

buildings.name: Shop Arcade
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 10 m grid with glass barrel roofs over the two arcades.
buildings.look: Two three-storey shop bars with glass barrel roofs over their arcades, warm shopfront light spilling out, linked by bridges across an open middle court.
buildings.entrances: Arcade entrances at both ends, from the Concourse Road and from Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 90 shops; about 8,000 visitors at a time.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, service lanes at the back of the shops.
buildings.interior: Two shop bars, each with its own glass-roofed arcade: duty-free, travel goods, pharmacy, grocery, books and banking on the ground floor, fashion and electronics above, restaurants, a food court and a cinema on top.

buildings.name: Transit Lounges
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with stepped terraces, each floor set back over the one below.
buildings.look: A long building that steps back in three planted terraces toward the garden courts, with timber screens and soft lighting; quiet and calm after the terminals.
buildings.entrances: From the Concourse Road side and from the Concourse Promenade on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: About 6,000 travellers resting at a time; 360 sleep cabins.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, showers, sleep cabins by the hour.
buildings.interior: A long lounge building with the main transit lounge, showers, family lounge, prayer rooms and cafés on the ground floor, quiet and work lounges, sleep pods and a spa above, and a roof garden lounge; a pod hotel of sleep cabins behind it, and garden courts.

buildings.name: Market Hall
buildings.structure: Cast-steel arches spanning 320 m (1,050 ft) under a glass-and-timber vault, 21 m (69 ft) high.
buildings.look: A great vaulted market hall of arched steel ribs and timber panels with a long glass roof, flanked by two lines of small shops; busy, warm and noisy.
buildings.entrances: Open market squares at both ends; shop doors on both long sides; deliveries from Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 300 stalls and 48 shops; about 10,000 visitors at a time.
buildings.services: 4 stair cores, cold rooms, waste and recycling yard.
buildings.interior: A vaulted market hall with fresh produce, bakers, butchers, spice, street food and flower stalls and a seating hall, two lines of shops with a cooking school and market offices above, open market squares at each end and a delivery yard.

buildings.name: Restaurant Row
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with timber floors; restaurants open onto the terrace with folding glass walls.
buildings.look: Two long rows of restaurants facing each other across a terrace and a lit water channel, each with its own coloured awning and roof garden bar.
buildings.entrances: Every restaurant opens onto the waterside terrace; deliveries from the service lane.
buildings.capacity: About 60 restaurants and bars; about 9,000 diners at a time.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, grease and waste lines, kitchen extract.
buildings.interior: Two rows of restaurants with private dining and bars upstairs, a music venue, and roof terrace bars, facing a waterside terrace and channel.

buildings.name: Travellers' Clinic
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid.
buildings.look: An L-shaped white clinic with green-tinted glass and a small healing garden in its corner.
buildings.entrances: Walk-in entrance from the Concourse Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,500 patients a day; 40 short-stay beds.
buildings.interior: A walk-in clinic with vaccination rooms, pharmacy, consulting rooms, a travel health lab and a short-stay ward, and a side wing with dental, eye, imaging and physio clinics round a garden.

buildings.name: Concourse Police Post
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete frame with a hardened ground floor.
buildings.look: A long two-storey charcoal block with a blue light band and a glass front desk facing the concourse.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance from the Concourse Road; vehicle yard behind.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, CCTV room covering the concourse.
buildings.interior: Front desk, interview and holding rooms, lost property and garage below; open office, CCTV room and briefing room above.

buildings.name: Grand Port Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete core towers with flat slabs on a two-storey steel and stone podium.
buildings.look: The port's flagship: two slim 80 m (263 ft) towers of champagne-tinted glass with bronze fins rising from a long white stone podium, joined at the top by lit sky lounges; a grand entrance court with a fountain on Hotel Row.
buildings.entrances: Grand entrance court on Hotel Row; garden entrance on the Station Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,200 guest rooms (from the brief), in two towers of 17 guest floors.
buildings.services: 8 stair and lift cores, ballroom, spa and pool, sky bar.
buildings.interior: A two-storey podium with grand lobby, restaurants, bar, shops, ballroom, meeting rooms, spa and pool, and two guest towers of 17 floors each with a sky bar and sky restaurant on top; hotel gardens behind.

buildings.name: Harbour Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete flat-slab wings, eight storeys on the long sides and six on the short sides.
buildings.look: A mid-range courtyard hotel in white render and blue-grey metal balconies, wrapped around a big garden with a pool; striped awnings on the ground-floor restaurant.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the drop-off on Hotel Row.
buildings.services: 10 stair and lift cores, pool, gym, meeting rooms.
buildings.interior: Four wings round a garden and pool: lobby, restaurant and bar at the front, meeting rooms and gym at the back, guest rooms on every floor above.

buildings.name: Crew Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete flat-slab slabs, ten storeys, joined by a two-storey link.
buildings.look: Two plain, neat ten-storey slabs in pale grey with coloured window panels for each airline crew floor, joined by a glass link.
buildings.entrances: Drop-off and entrance on Hotel Row.
buildings.services: 5 stair and lift cores, 24-hour canteen, shuttle bus to the gates.
buildings.interior: Two crew room slabs with reception, canteen, laundry, lounge and gym on the ground floors, joined by a link with a shuttle bus lounge.

buildings.name: Port Hostel
buildings.structure: Modular steel-frame capsule floors on a concrete ground floor.
buildings.look: A bright, cheerful six-storey block in orange and white panels with a lit roof deck and a courtyard full of tables.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, shared kitchen and bathrooms.
buildings.interior: Reception, common kitchen and common room below, four floors of capsule rooms, and a roof deck; a courtyard and a bike and pod stand behind.

buildings.name: Concourse Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant floors with blast walls; steel roof.
buildings.look: Plain graphite sheds with tall louvres and a round-topped water tank.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and water for P6; about 25 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, chillers, air handling, water pumps.
buildings.interior: A substation, a plant hall with chillers, air handling and water pumps, and a water tank.

buildings.name: Concourse Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A tall graphite head house with yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the Station Road side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: A vehicle lift, a goods lift and a hotel supplies lift.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with three lifts down to the service layer.
